overview: Intuit is a global financial technology platform that helps consumers, small and mid-market businesses, and accountants manage their financial lives, best known for TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp. The company describes itself as an 'AI-driven expert platform' combining data, AI, and human tax/financial experts to automate everyday financial tasks (tax filing, bookkeeping, payroll, payments, marketing, credit/lending). Intuit operates primarily in the U.S. with a growing international QuickBooks/Mailchimp footprint, and reports fiscal years ending July 31 (FY2026 ended July 31, 2026).

business_model.summary: Intuit monetizes four large, largely subscription/transaction-based franchises: QuickBooks (small/mid-market accounting, payroll, payments - subscription plus transaction/interchange revenue), TurboTax (seasonal DIY/assisted tax prep - transactional, concentrated in Q2-Q3 fiscal quarters), Credit Karma (consumer credit monitoring monetized via cost-per-action/cost-per-click lead generation to lenders/insurers), and Mailchimp (SMB email/marketing automation - subscription). Reporting segments are Global Business Solutions (QuickBooks, Mailchimp through FY2026, payments/payroll), Consumer (TurboTax, Credit Karma, ProTax), with Mailchimp becoming its own reportable segment starting FY2027.
business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2C and B2B/SMB - consumers (TurboTax, Credit Karma), small businesses and self-employed (QuickBooks Online, payroll, payments), mid-market businesses ($10M-$100M+ revenue via Intuit Enterprise Suite/QuickBooks Advanced), and professional accountants (ProTax, QuickBooks Accountant)
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly United States; QuickBooks and Mailchimp have international operations (UK, Canada, Australia, and other markets) but the large majority of revenue is U.S.-sourced

competitive_position.market_position: Dominant leader: TurboTax holds roughly 60%+ of the U.S. DIY consumer tax prep market; QuickBooks holds an estimated ~80% share of small business accounting software in the U.S. Credit Karma is one of the largest consumer credit-monitoring platforms with over 100 million members. Mailchimp is a leading SMB email marketing platform but faces intensifying competition from lower-cost and AI-native alternatives.

moat_factors.description: QuickBooks embeds itself in a business's books, payroll, and payments; accountants are trained on and recommend the platform, creating high data-migration and workflow switching costs
Large QuickBooks user base attracts third-party app developers and ProAdvisor accountants, which in turn reinforces the platform's value to end customers
TurboTax and QuickBooks are category-defining brands with decades of consumer/SMB trust in a compliance-sensitive category (tax filing, bookkeeping)
Combining TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp data lets Intuit target financial offers and insights; ARPU is ~30% higher for customers using both TurboTax and Credit Karma
Constant U.S. federal/state tax code changes and payroll/compliance requirements favor an incumbent with deep integration and update infrastructure over new entrants

weaknesses: TurboTax revenue is highly seasonal and concentrated in a few months, creating volatility and reliance on a successful tax season
Reputational and regulatory overhang from 'free' filing marketing practices (FTC order, state settlements) creates headline/legal risk
Mailchimp growth has stalled/gone negative, diluting the growth profile versus QuickBooks and Credit Karma
Heavy U.S. concentration limits diversification versus more globally diversified SaaS peers
Low-cost/free alternatives (FreeTaxUSA, other DIY tools) and AI chatbots threaten to commoditize simple tax-prep and bookkeeping tasks over time

growth_drivers: AI-native product suite (Intuit Assist, Intuit Intelligence Chat, agentic AI features) embedded across TurboTax, QuickBooks, and Enterprise Suite to automate bookkeeping, tax prep, and financial decision-making

Mid-market expansion via Intuit Enterprise Suite targeting an estimated $89 billion market of businesses with ~$10M-$100M+ in revenue that have outgrown QuickBooks but don't want a costly traditional ERP; QuickBooks Online Advanced + Enterprise Suite revenue grew ~38% YoY in Q3 FY2026

Credit Karma monetization expansion (personal loans, auto insurance, credit cards) growing high-teens percent annually and deepening TurboTax cross-sell (54% increase in tax filers starting their filing journey through Credit Karma)
QuickBooks payments and payroll attach rates (embedded fintech/money movement) driving higher revenue per customer beyond subscription fees
International QuickBooks expansion in English-speaking and other markets
Mailchimp cross-sell into the QuickBooks customer base and eventual reacceleration as its own reportable segment starting FY2027

Organizational restructuring (2026 workforce reduction, ~17%/3,000 roles) intended to simplify structure and reallocate investment toward AI product development, including partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI

business.description: IRS Direct File was discontinued for the 2026 filing season after Intuit and industry lobbying, removing a nascent free-file competitive threat, but political and public pressure for government-provided free filing could resurface in future years and remains a structural risk to TurboTax's low-end pricing power
Free/low-cost DIY alternatives (FreeTaxUSA, TaxSlayer) and AI chatbots could erode TurboTax pricing and market share over time as simple tax filing becomes commoditized
Mailchimp revenue growth has slowed to roughly flat/negative, and competitive pressure from other marketing automation and AI-native tools is intense
The 2026 workforce reduction (~17% of employees) and reorganization around AI could disrupt product roadmaps, customer support, and morale during the transition

financial.description: FY2026 restructuring generated $300-340 million in charges, pressuring near-term GAAP margins versus non-GAAP results
Premium valuation leaves limited room for execution missteps or growth deceleration to be absorbed without significant share price impact

regulatory.risk: FTC 'free' advertising order and consumer protection scrutiny
regulatory.description: A 2024 FTC Opinion and Final Order restricts how Intuit can advertise 'free' TurboTax offerings; past state settlements ($141 million multistate settlement in 2022) demonstrate ongoing legal/regulatory exposure around marketing practices

Although IRS Direct File was shelved for 2026, the program's code was open-sourced, and future administrations or state-level programs could revive free government tax filing, threatening TurboTax's addressable market and pricing

Intuit holds vast troves of sensitive financial and tax data across TurboTax, Credit Karma, and QuickBooks; evolving U.S. state privacy laws and AI governance rules could raise compliance costs or restrict data monetization
Credit Karma operates in a regulated space (lending referrals, credit reporting); CFPB or state-level rule changes could affect its cost-per-action business model

macro.risk: Interest rate sensitivity via Credit Karma
macro.description: Credit Karma's revenue depends on lender/insurer marketing budgets and loan origination volumes, which are sensitive to interest rates and consumer credit cycles

macro.risk: SMB formation and economic cycle exposure
macro.description: QuickBooks and payments revenue are tied to small business formation, employment, and transaction volumes, which soften in a recession
TurboTax upsells (Live, Full Service) and Mailchimp subscriptions could see downgrades if consumers and small businesses tighten spending

macro_factors.industry_outlook: SMB accounting/fintech software and consumer tax-prep software markets are expected to continue growing at high-single to double-digit rates, driven by digitization of small business finance, embedded fintech (payments/payroll), and AI-enabled automation reducing manual bookkeeping and filing work
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - TurboTax and Credit Karma have some sensitivity to consumer/credit cycles and tax-law changes; QuickBooks subscription revenue is more resilient but transaction/payments revenue scales with SMB economic activity
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - primarily indirect via Credit Karma's dependence on lending/insurance origination volumes, which are rate-sensitive, and via SMB borrowing/spending behavior
key_input_costs: Cloud infrastructure/data center costs (AWS and other hosting)
AI compute costs (partnerships with Anthropic, OpenAI)
Customer acquisition/marketing spend (especially seasonal TurboTax advertising)

recent_developments.event: Reported Q4 and full fiscal year 2026 results: FY2026 total revenue grew 14% to $21.4 billion; Q4 revenue grew 14% to $4.4 billion; GAAP EPS grew 20% to $16.46 and non-GAAP EPS grew 20% to $24.27 for the quarter; set FY2027 guidance

Announced restructuring to cut approximately 3,000 roles (~17% of workforce) to simplify the organization and refocus investment on AI products; incurred $300-340 million in restructuring charges, with signed AI partnerships including Anthropic and OpenAI
Raised full-year revenue guidance after strong Q3 results; QuickBooks Online Advanced plus Intuit Enterprise Suite revenue grew approximately 38% YoY, underscoring traction in the mid-market push

IRS confirmed that Direct File, the government's free tax-filing pilot, would not be available for the 2026 filing season, removing a nascent competitive/regulatory threat to TurboTax after years of industry lobbying; IRS subsequently open-sourced the Direct File codebase

Continued expansion of agentic AI features (Intuit Assist, Intuit Intelligence Chat) across TurboTax, QuickBooks, and Intuit Enterprise Suite aimed at proactive, done-for-you financial workflows for mid-market CFOs and accounting firms

Mailchimp began being managed as a separate operating unit from Global Business Solutions, becoming its own reportable segment starting in fiscal 2027, reflecting continued softness in Mailchimp growth relative to QuickBooks and Credit Karma

items.notes: Implies 9-10% YoY growth off the FY2026 base of $21.4 billion
Implies 13-14% growth, reflecting continued QuickBooks Online and mid-market/Enterprise Suite momentum
Implies 4-6% growth across TurboTax, Credit Karma, and ProTax
Implies -1% to 0% growth; first year reported as a standalone segment, reflecting ongoing softness
Implies 23-24% growth versus FY2026 non-GAAP EPS
Implies 22-24% growth; gap versus non-GAAP driven primarily by stock-based compensation and amortization of acquired intangibles

guidance.management_commentary: Management (CEO Sasan Goodarzi) framed FY2026's restructuring as a deliberate 'reset' to simplify the organization and accelerate AI-native product development across TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp, while continuing to emphasize the mid-market Intuit Enterprise Suite opportunity (addressing an estimated $89 billion market) as a key multi-year growth vector alongside Credit Karma monetization and QuickBooks payments/payroll attach.

bull_case: Dominant, sticky market positions in both consumer tax prep (~60%+ DIY share) and small business accounting (~80% share) provide a wide moat and pricing power

AI-native product strategy (Intuit Assist, Intelligence Chat, agentic workflows) could materially expand wallet share by automating higher-value bookkeeping, tax, and advisory tasks rather than just being disrupted by AI
Mid-market expansion via Intuit Enterprise Suite taps a large underserved $89 billion market and is already growing revenue ~38% YoY in that cohort, offering a long runway beyond core SMB QuickBooks
Credit Karma provides a high-margin, fast-growing (mid-to-high teens) monetization engine with strong cross-sell synergies into TurboTax, lifting blended ARPU
IRS Direct File being shelved for 2026 removes a key regulatory/competitive overhang on TurboTax's addressable market and pricing, at least in the near term
FY2027 guidance implies continued double-digit revenue growth (9-10%) and strong EPS growth (22-24%), well above most large-cap software peers
bear_case: IRS Direct File and other free-file initiatives remain a latent political/regulatory risk that could resurface and structurally cap TurboTax's low-end pricing and market share over the long term
Mailchimp's stagnant-to-declining growth (guided -1% to 0% for FY2027) is a drag on the overall growth profile and signals competitive weakness in marketing automation/SMB tools
Large-scale 2026 restructuring (~17% of workforce) introduces execution risk around product delivery, customer support quality, and employee morale during an AI transition
Premium valuation multiple leaves limited room for error; any deceleration in QuickBooks, Credit Karma, or mid-market Enterprise Suite growth could trigger material multiple compression

Ongoing regulatory/reputational risk from past 'free' TurboTax marketing practices (FTC order, prior state settlements) could resurface in the form of new litigation, fines, or forced changes to marketing and pricing practices

Heavy U.S. revenue concentration and seasonality (especially TurboTax's tax-season dependency) leave earnings more exposed to U.S.-specific regulatory, economic, and consumer credit cycles than more globally diversified SaaS peers
